subject: Procurement readiness & budget-owner mapping for Redwood POC
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chan <emily@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: procurement path discussion + next steps

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep procurement moving on your side:

Summary of call:
- Scope: 6-week POC for inference latency testing and cost model assessment across two customer workloads.
- Estimated POC value (list price): $28,500 (one-time for dedicated trial capacity) — likely falls into your PO flow.

Procurement / commercial items we discussed: 
- Payment preference: PO for >$25k; card for smaller pilot charges. Confirmed you usually use PO for production and larger POCs.
- Marketplace: you asked about AWS Marketplace listing — Redwood can list, but it typically adds time to onboarding.
- Docs needed: SOW, vendor packet, standard procurement questionnaire. I attached a short procurement qualifier for your team to complete (procurement-qualifier.xlsx).

Action items / ask from BrightLeaf:
1) Confirm preferred payment method for this POC (PO vs card) and whether AWS Marketplace is a requirement.
2) Provide the single procurement contact (name + email) and the budget owner / economic buyer who will approve the line item.
3) Any required vendor packet fields we should pre-fill (tax ID, legal address, insurance limits).

Next steps from Redwood:
- I will send an editable SOW template and a PO-friendly SOW variant (attach: SOW-Redwood-PO-option.pdf).
- Vivek will prepare a short technical appendix for procurement (latency SLA, data handling).

Proposed follow-up: 30-min sync early next week to walk procurement through the packet if helpful.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187
From: Emily Chan <emily@brightleafhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: procurement path discussion + next steps

Thanks, Karthik — great summary. A few clarifications from procurement side:

- Payment: Correct — for anything > $25,000 we push through a PO and need a signed SOW. For small pilots we sometimes do corporate card but approvals take longer. The $28.5k POC will almost certainly be PO.
- Marketplace: We prefer Marketplace for ongoing contracted spend, but for initial POCs we can do direct vendor PO to accelerate. Marketplace introduces procurement lead time (legal + registration) — not ideal for a March/April rollout.
- Procurement contact: procurement@brightleafhealth.com is our shared mailbox. Primary procurement reviewer: Rajesh Banerjee (Rajesh.Banerjee@brightleafhealth.com), VP Finance.
- Budget / economic owner: The product org is sponsoring this pilot — Alyssa Green (Alyssa.Green@brightleafhealth.com), Director of Product, is the budget owner. Final signatory for >$25k is our CFO (Anna Morales).

I'll share the procurement-qualifier with Rajesh and ask for any specific vendor packet fields. If you can send the PO-style SOW, I'll route it to procurement and finance for a quick prereview.

Emily

--
Emily Chan
Sr Product Manager, BrightLeaf Health
emily@brightleafhealth.com | (617) 555-0199
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chan <emily@brightleafhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: procurement path discussion + next steps

Emily — perfect, that's exactly the mapping we need. Based on what you shared, here's the commercial path I'm proposing and the items we'll prepare this week:

Commercial path (recommended):
- Pilot (PO route): we will prepare a PO-friendly SOW and vendor packet. Because the POC is above your $25k threshold, procurement + finance signoff will be required.
- Fast path option: if timing is tight, we can temporarily accept a card for the initial 2-week kick-off and then convert to PO for the remainder — this helps unblock technical work while paperwork completes.
- Marketplace: hold off for now; pursue after successful pilot to avoid onboarding delays.

Who we need on your side:
- Budget owner / economic buyer: Alyssa Green — include her on the SOW distribution for approval.
- Finance sponsor / final signatory: Anna Morales (CFO) — procurement will route to her.
- Procurement reviewer: Rajesh Banerjee — procurement@brightleafhealth.com will handle standard checks.

What I'll send today:
1) PO-style SOW (SOW-Redwood-PO-option.pdf).
2) Completed vendor fields (tax ID, Redwood legal address, insurance summary).
3) Short technical appendix from Vivek (attached inline in email).

Could you please confirm two items so we can pre-fill the SOW before sending to Rajesh: 
A) Legal entity name and billing address for BrightLeaf to appear on the SOW (if different from company header).
B) Typical PO routing time (estimate) and any required PO number format we should honor.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 20-min handoff with Rajesh and Anna next Tue to walk through the SOW.

Appreciate it — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Hi Karthik/Emily — Rajesh is OOO until Monday but quick note from procurement team: 

- We received the PO-style SOW and vendor fields; please send to procurement@brightleafhealth.com with the subject line 'PO Request: Redwood Inference — BLH POC'.
- Preferred signing flow: DocuSign routing to Anna Morales (CFO) for signature after finance review.
- Typical internal lead time: 5–8 business days once procurement has the finalized SOW and insurance docs. If Alyssa (budget owner) signs off quickly we can expedite to ~3 business days.

We'll log the request when Rajesh returns Monday and assign a ticket. If you want faster turnaround, include a short executive summary in the body of your PO request email calling out the business justification and expected go-live.

Thanks — procurement team
